messages.text: Crystal Palace Women deducted three points for use of subs

metadata.summary: Crystal Palace Women have been deducted three points in the WSL with immediate effect.
metadata.content: Crystal Palace Women deducted three points in WSL for making substitutions at four windows in Everton win | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Crystal Palace Women deducted three points in WSL for making substitutions at four windows in Everton win Crystal Palace Women are being punished for making substitutions at four separate windows in a win over Everton in September - the last of which came in the 97th minute - which is in breach of IFAB Laws that state clubs have no more than three substitution opportunities in each match Tuesday 24 November 2026 11:47, UK Crystal Palace Women have been deducted three points in the WSL with immediate effect. Palace, who now drop into the relegation play-off spot, are being punished for making substitutions at four separate windows in a 1-0 win over Everton in September. This is in breach of IFAB Laws, which state clubs can make five substitutions, but have no more than three opportunities in each match to do so. Palace made a substitution in a fourth window in the 97th minute of the match. Kirsty Howat, who was brought on for Shannon O'Brien, did not touch the ball before the full-time whistle was blown. messages.text: Commanders upset Burrow's Bengals after last-second winner

metadata.summary: Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens' 26-yard field goal as time expired as the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night.
metadata.content: NFL: Washington Commanders beat Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals in upset after last-second field goal from Drew Stevens | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL: Washington Commanders beat Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals in upset after last-second field goal from Drew Stevens Drew Stevens kicks last-second field goal to lift Washington Commanders to surprise win over Joe Burrow's high-flying Cincinnati Bengals; watch an NFL Thanksgiving triple-header live on Sky Sports NFL from 5pm on Thursday Sky Sports Tuesday 24 November 2026 06:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Cincinnati Bengals against the Washington Commanders from Week 11 of the NFL season. Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens' 26-yard field goal as time expired as the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night. After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight. The Commanders quarterback spiked it with five seconds left and Stevens did the rest. metadata.content: Dalton Smith: Paths align better for Shakur Stevenson unification than Adam Azim fight | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Dalton Smith: Paths align better for Shakur Stevenson unification than Adam Azim fight Dalton Smith has had an outstanding 2026, winning and defending the WBC super-lightweight world title with wins over Subriel Matias and Alberto Puello; Smith believes he can headline at Hillsborough Stadium in his Sheffield hometown with American star Shakur Stevenson a potential opponent Monday 23 November 2026 14:23, UK Image: Dalton Smith successfully defended his WBC title with a split decision victory over Alberto Puello Dalton Smith, the WBC super-lightweight champion, thinks he's more likely to fight Shakur Stevenson next than Adam Azim. Sheffield's Smith has had an outstanding year, knocking out Subriel Matias in New York to win his world championship and defending the belt against Alberto Puello in his Sheffield hometown. American star Shakur Stevenson secured the WBO's super-lightweight championship when he beat Teofimo Lopez in January. Both Smith and Stevenson are looking for their next opponents and a unification between the pair would be an appealing match up.
